title: Russian woman uses AI photo to prank friend, gets fined for setting off bear alarm
key_facts: A court in Russia's Far East fined a woman 15,000 roubles ($178).
She lives in Magdagachi, Amur region, and used ChatGPT to make an image of a large brown bear walking down a local street, which she sent to a friend in September as a joke.
The image spread through messaging apps, residents called police, and the district head sent wildlife rangers to search for the non-existent bear.
She later called police and admitted making the image.
In mid-September a woman in the Transbaikal region was fined 30,000 roubles for a fake bear image, per RAPSI.
At least 26 people have been killed in bear attacks since spring (RIA Novosti); the bear population is 308,000, more than doubled in 30 years.
quote_evidence: "The joke quickly got out of control. The photograph of the bear spread through messaging apps, and police began receiving alarmed calls from residents," the Amur courts' press service said.
A court ordered her this week to pay the fine of 15,000 roubles.
It was the second such case reported in Russia within a few weeks.
why_it_matters_hint: Fake AI images now trigger real searches and fines where fear of real attacks is high.
event_date: Image sent in September 2026; fine ordered week of 12 Oct 2026
